bug_description.original: A stack-buffer-overflow occurs in the function simple_str_to_doublestr.
bug_description.normalized: When libical parses the staged text `BEGIN:\nGEo:.................................`, the second line is admitted as a GEO property and its value after the colon is copied into a temporary 33-byte dot string. `icalvalue_new_from_string_with_error()` then enters the GEO parser and passes that string into `simple_str_to_doublestr()` with `geo.lat`, a 16-byte stack array, as the destination. The vulnerable helper scans all 33 dots as the first coordinate token, checks only whether the token length plus NUL exceeds 100, and then copies all 33 bytes into `geo.lat`. That byte-wise copy overruns `geo.lat`, overwrites the adjacent `geo.lon`, and writes one byte past the 32-byte `geo` stack object, which AddressSanitizer reports as a stack-buffer-overflow write in `simple_str_to_doublestr`.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled `GEo:` content line. It materializes the property-name token and advances `end` to the start of the GEO value substring that later reaches the overflow.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the 44-byte text `BEGIN:\nGEo:.................................`. On the second line, `line` points at `GEo:.................................` when this statement runs.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call copies the entire GEO property value into a standalone string buffer. For the witness, that buffer is exactly 33 `.` characters followed by NUL, and it later becomes the `from` argument to `simple_str_to_doublestr`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: At this point `end` already points just past the colon in `GEo:.................................`, so the returned string is the exact substring `.................................`.
tainted_value_origin.note: `strstriplt(str)` immediately afterward leaves the string unchanged because it contains no leading or trailing whitespace.

root_cause.description: The only pre-copy size check is destination-independent: it rejects coordinate substrings longer than 99 bytes but does not compare against the actual destination buffer length. The 34-byte token-with-NUL therefore passes even though `result` aliases `geo.lat[16]`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by adding a `result_len` parameter to `simple_str_to_doublestr()` and passing `ICAL_GEO_LEN` from both GEO call sites.

sink.description: Byte write inside the latitude-copy loop. With the witness token length of 33 and `result == geo.lat`, this assignment overruns the 16-byte destination and writes one byte past the enclosing 32-byte `geo` stack object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports a 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow write in `simple_str_to_doublestr` and identifies the caller's `geo` stack object as the overflowed frame object.

parser_admitted.description: On the `GEo:` line this early error path is bypassed because the preceding `BEGIN:` line already left a component on the parser stack. That admits the property-name and property-value parsing path below.

coarse_trace.summary: The second content line is parsed as a property: `GEo` is recognized as a GEO property and the entire value after the colon is copied into a separate 33-dot string.

The GEO-value branch zero-initializes `struct icalgeotype geo`, whose `lat` and `lon` fields are both 16-byte arrays, and passes the attacker-controlled value string into `simple_str_to_doublestr()` for latitude parsing.
The helper scans all 33 dots as one latitude token and keeps it because its only size guard is `end - start + 1 > 100`, not a check against the 16-byte destination buffer.

The byte-copy loop writes the entire 33-byte token into `geo.lat`, overwrites `geo.lon`, and writes one byte past the 32-byte `geo` stack object, matching the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow write.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the second input line `GEo:.................................`, this call extracts `str == "GEo"` and advances `end` to the first `.` after the colon, creating the property parser state that the vulnerable GEO path uses.

The extracted property-name token is converted into the property kind used for downstream dispatch. On the witness path this resolves the mixed-case name `GEo` to the GEO property kind that later selects GEO value parsing.

The property kind from step 2 is translated into the default value parser kind. For this property, `value_kind` becomes `ICAL_GEO_VALUE`, routing the property contents into the GEO branch in `icalvalue_new_from_string_with_error()`.

Tainted value origin. This copies the full substring after the colon into a standalone value buffer. For the witness, `str` becomes 33 `.` characters plus NUL, and the later `strstriplt(str)` does not change it because there is no whitespace to trim.
The GEO branch zero-initializes the destination object before parsing coordinates. `ICAL_GEO_LEN` is 16, so `geo.lat` and `geo.lon` are adjacent 16-byte arrays inside one 32-byte stack `geo` object.

The extracted 33-dot GEO value is passed as the `from` string to `simple_str_to_doublestr()`, and the fixed 16-byte `geo.lat` array is passed as `result`. This binds the attacker-controlled coordinate token to the stack destination before any semicolon or longitude checks run.

There is no leading whitespace, so `start == from`. The scan treats `.` as valid coordinate text and consumes all 33 dots until the terminating NUL, producing `end - start == 33`; no `;` delimiter is encountered before the copy phase.

Root cause. The function compares the 33-byte token plus NUL against the constant 100 instead of the actual destination size. The witness therefore passes this guard with length 34 even though `result` still aliases the 16-byte `geo.lat` buffer from step 6.

Sink. Because `from == start`, the loop bound is 33. Iterations 0-15 fill `geo.lat`, iterations 16-31 overwrite `geo.lon`, and iteration 32 writes one byte past the 32-byte `geo` stack object. AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow write in this function and names the caller's `geo` frame object.

poc.trigger: Parse the staged text `BEGIN:\nGEo:.................................` with `icalparser_parse_string()`. The GEO parser copies the 33-dot first coordinate into `geo.lat[16]` and AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow write in `simple_str_to_doublestr`.

format.name: iCalendar text
format.contract: The text must reach property parsing inside a component context and include a `GEO` content line whose entire value is the exact 33-dot string `.................................`, with no leading whitespace and no `;` delimiter before end of line.
